answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x-1|$, with vertex $(1,0)$, then translate it down 2 units to obtain $y=|x-1|-2$, with vertex $(1,-2)$.

Find its $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}|x-1|-2&=0\\|x-1|&=2\\x&=-1\text{ or }x=3.\end{align*}$$
Reflect the portion below the $x$-axis upwards. The final graph has sharp turning points at $(-1,0)$, $(1,2)$ and $(3,0)$, with both outer branches rising.

At $x=0$,
$$y=\bigl||0-1|-2\bigr|=1,$$
so the $y$-intercept is $(0,1)$.
